Lemma
[first-order form of the Jacobi equation]

Source: petersen:page-0116 ↗ def:pet-ch3-jacobi-field

$\mathcal L_{\partial _r}J=0$ is equivalent to $ abla _{\partial _r}J=S(J)$, and consequently $\operatorname {Hess}r(J,J)=g( abla _{\partial _r}J,J)= frac 12\partial _rg(J,J)$.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch3-jacobi-field-equivalent-equation

\sketch Torsion-freeness gives $\mathcal L_{\partial _r}J=[\partial _r,J] = abla _{\partial _r}J- abla _J\partial _r = abla _{\partial _r}J-S(J)$. Pairing the resulting equation with $J$ proves the Hessian and length identity.

□
